solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: High water streak formed by its fin?

definitions.text: High water streak formed by its fin?

indicators.note: formed says the letters of the preceding phrase are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A wake or streak across the sea made by a shark's dorsal fin cutting through the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of HIGH WATER STREAK rearrange to the answer, and the streak a dorsal fin cuts through the sea is exactly what this predator leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: This large predatory shark is famous for the triangular dorsal fin slicing the surface of the sea.

clue.text: An occasion when everyone gets cross?

definitions.text: An occasion when everyone gets cross?

parts.words: An occasion when everyone gets cross?
parts.note: voters mark a cross on the ballot paper, so everyone puts down a cross rather than getting angry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' seems to mean angry, but it is the X each voter marks on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationwide vote for a parliament is when the whole electorate marks crosses on ballots.

clue.text: Without leads, Dench can't beguile

indicators.note: the leads of the two words are their first letters, and both are dropped

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Without star billing, the actress Judi Dench is somehow unable to charm the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without leads' removes the first letter of both Dench and can't, leaving ENCH and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant someone is to charm or captivate them, a close synonym of beguile.

clue.text: Tenacity of Untouchables leader, strong up front

indicators.note: up front says the word for strong is placed before the other piece in this down answer

parts.note: tough means strong, resilient
Eliot Ness led the team of agents known as the Untouchables against Al Capone

explanation.surface: A tribute to the doggedness of the man who led the Untouchables, a strong man always out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot Ness headed the Prohibition agents nicknamed the Untouchables in 1930s Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity and toughness both describe the resilience to keep going under pressure.

clue.text: Dye chicken (North American)

parts.note: a hen is a female chicken
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: Reads like a menu item or a recipe: dyed chicken, North American style.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown plant dye used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Top Trade Union bloke at home, eating heartily

parts.note: the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is the top body of British trade unions
a king is a man, as in the king or man piece in chess or cards; here simply a chap
in means at home

explanation.surface: A senior union official at home, enjoying a hearty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC (Trades Union Congress) is the British umbrella body for trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: To tuck in is an informal idiom for eating with gusto and appetite.

clue.text: Oops! Upset following parody

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word over, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone apologises after causing offence with a satirical send-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a humorous imitation or send-up, the same thing as a parody.

clue.text: Sinatra…amazing craftsman

indicators.note: amazing, in its sense of bewildering, signals the singer's name is jumbled

explanation.surface: Praise for Frank Sinatra as a masterly craftsman of song.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things by hand.

clue.text: Stay cool and don't get one's back sunburnt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom urging someone to keep calm and not lose their temper
second meaning, taken literally: keep a garment on to protect one's back from the sun

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for calming down is read literally as advice to keep your top on in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells an angry person to remain calm; literally, keeping a garment on protects the skin.

clue.text: A section of the church service reportedly criticised the Ashes trophy

definitions.text: A section of the church service

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is heard rather than read, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: knocked means criticised; the Ashes, the England v Australia cricket series, is played for a tiny urn

explanation.surface: A cricket fan rails against the Ashes trophy during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia; its trophy is a small urn. KNOCKED URN said quickly gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturn is one of the divisions of the night office of matins in the Catholic liturgy.

clue.text: Time left stuck in boring job? That's a laugh!

indicators.note: stuck in means the two letters are wedged inside the other piece

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the idea of spending time stuck in a dull job.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a kind of laugh.

clue.text: Communicate with Republican individually…

parts.note: each means individually, one by one

explanation.surface: An instruction to contact Republicans one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach someone is to get in touch, contacting them by phone or message.

clue.text: …albeit regularly shifty, fidgety, suspicious

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of albeit, starting from the first
fidgety, restless and twitching, signals the letters of shifty are jumbled

explanation.surface: A description of a nervous character who seems shifty and fidgety, and thus dubious.
explanation.walkthrough: This clue continues from 11 across with its ellipsis, but the parse stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something a bit fishy seems dubious or questionable, an informal idiom for slightly suspect.

clue.text: Big turtle on the loose — he leaves an ugly mess

indicators.note: on the loose means running free and disordered, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An escaped giant turtle trashes everything in its path.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug is someone who drops rubbish carelessly in public places.

clue.text: Private waxwork of Neymar?

parts.note: a waxing of the private parts takes its name from a South American country, which is also the nationality of the footballer Neymar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Waxwork' suggests a Madame Tussauds statue, but it is waxing work on private parts; Neymar is a footballer from the same country that names that wax.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a style of intimate hair-removal wax and the nationality of footballer Neymar.

clue.text: Brahmin husband elected Democrat Unionist

parts.note: in means elected, as a party voted in
DU stands for Democratic Unionist, as in Northern Ireland's DUP

explanation.surface: A news snippet: a man of high caste marries and wins a seat for Northern Ireland's unionists.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahmins form the priestly caste within the religion followed by most Indians.

clue.text: The masses vote in dodgy Ohio Independent

indicators.note: in places the word for vote inside the jumbled state name
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the state's letters are not as written

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Ordinary voters back a shady independent candidate in an Ohio election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is the container signal; the masses are the common people, not a vote count.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is a Greek-derived term for the common people or general populace.

clue.text: City is winning, according to the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so this signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: leads means is ahead, is winning

explanation.surface: A football commentator on the radio reports that City are ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like a team such as Manchester City, but it is the definition: a city in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: People leaving corrupt regimes?

indicators.note: corrupt, as in debased or altered, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refugees flee from corrupt governments.
explanation.definitionFit: Émigrés are those who have left their native country, usually for political reasons.

clue.text: Working Tunisian receiving electronic payments on a regular basis

indicators.note: receiving means one piece takes the other inside it
working, like something being worked over, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A Tunisian worker is paid electronically on a regular schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed sum paid yearly, often bought with a pension pot.

clue.text: Somewhat nicer in Kyiv, but it's cold!

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Life in Kyiv is somewhat pleasanter, but the weather is cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice rink is a skating surface kept frozen, so it is necessarily chilly.

clue.text: Cold fish skin wrap?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ling is a type of fish related to the cod
a film is a thin skin or layer

explanation.surface: Instructions to wrap a cold fish's skin, as if packing leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cling film is the thin plastic used to wrap and cover food.

clue.text: Radical feminist starts to go round every English region

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A radical feminist sets out to tour every region of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is an Australian-born feminist, author of The Female Eunuch.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer is a celebrated and outspoken feminist writer of the second-wave movement.

clue.text: Set up 101 total, which is pleasing to hear

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
a sum is a total

explanation.surface: Someone tots up a total of 101 and is pleased by the figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reads the pieces upwards because this is a down clue; 101 is a Roman numeral, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is organised sound that delights the ear, as in 'music to my ears'.

clue.text: Job, Elijah packing daggers

indicators.note: packing means the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first name into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Two Old Testament prophets carry concealed blades.
explanation.walkthrough: Obeli is the plural of obelus, the dagger symbol used in print for footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: The obelus is the typographic mark † , known to printers as a dagger.

clue.text: Serial criminal, international citizen from the Middle East

indicators.note: criminal, as in crooked, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A serial offender with international reach, wanted in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a national of Israel, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Well, Ms Lane…debut of talented individual musician

parts.note: so is used like 'well' to start a remark
Lois Lane is Superman's reporter girlfriend

indicators.note: the debut of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone muses about a reporter called Ms Lane making a talented solo debut.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist performs alone, a single performer rather than part of an ensemble.

clue.text: Wonky hip concerns King, not a young man any more

definitions.text: not a young man any more

indicators.note: wonky means crooked and off-kilter, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A monarch's dodgy hip is causing worries, signalling his advancing years.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who is past their youthful prime.
